column1: Mountains form over billions of years as huge pieces of Earth’s surface [called tectonic plates] are pushed together
column2: causing rock to crumple and push upwards. Mountains can also form when lava flows out from inside the Earth and cools on the surface adding new layers of rock. Mountains can appear sharp

column10:
A mountain is a natural landform that rises high above the land around it. Mountains are found all over the world and often have trees and plants growing between the rocks down the sides. The highest places on Earth are the tops of mountains–which are called peaks. It can be very cold at the peak–so cold that year-round some mountains are covered with snow or sheets of ice called glaciers. [Many rivers begin as water flowing down mountains] Many mountains are so large that they stop clouds from passing by and affect the weather on either side–often leaving one side with wetter forests and the other side drier deserts. 
When the Earth was forming, the surface was under constant change. So, there isn't a 'first' mountain, but scientists called geologists who study Earth’s surface found rocks in the Makhonhwa Mountains of South Africa and Eswatini that are over three billion years old.
